original_question: Let X ⊂ C^n be compact and totally disconnected. Assume that X has finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Then is X polynomially convex?
target_in_paper: Proposition 1.2, the introduction’s explicit reformulation of Conjecture 1.1: the paper reduces the conjecture to the case of compact totally disconnected sets of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure in complex Euclidean space.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s core reduced problem: a compact subset of complex Euclidean space, assumed totally disconnected and of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, and the question whether it must be polynomially convex. The ambient setting X ⊂ C^n and the conclusion about polynomial convexity are on target, and the finiteness hypothesis is stated in essentially the right measure-theoretic form.
missing_details: The paper’s formulation is presented as a reformulation/equivalent reduction of a broader conjecture, so the draft should indicate that this is the reduced form of Conjecture 1.1 rather than an isolated standalone question.
The notation for the measure should be made explicit as the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(X) < ∞.
The ambient dimension should be quantified as arbitrary complex Euclidean dimension n (equivalently N in the paper’s notation), not a fixed but unnamed ambient dimension.
The meaning of polynomially convex should be stated explicitly: X equals its polynomial hull \hat X = {z in C^n : |p(z)| <= sup_X |p| for every complex polynomial p}.

If one wants the question to be fully paper-faithful, one should note that the paper’s main conjecture is broader and concerns finite-length compact sets with no simple closed curve / vanishing first Cech cohomology; the totally disconnected version appears because Proposition 1.2 proves it is equivalent.
The draft does not mention that the paper uses this formulation as an equivalent reduction of Conjecture 1.1 and not as a broader generalization beyond the finite-length setting.
refined_question: Let n >= 1, and let X be a compact, totally disconnected subset of C^n with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(X) < ∞. Must X be polynomially convex; equivalently, is it true that \hat X = X, where \hat X := {z in C^n : |p(z)| <= sup_{x in X} |p(x)| for every complex polynomial p}?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation from Conjecture 1.1: if X ⊂ C^n is compact with H^1(X) < ∞ and X contains no simple closed curve (equivalently, in the paper’s cohomological version, has trivial first Cech cohomology), must X be polynomially convex?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual reduced problem, but the paper frames it as an equivalent reformulation of a broader conjecture in the introduction. The nearest official target is therefore Proposition 1.2 rather than replacing it by the broader conjecture itself. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must spell out the Hausdorff-measure notation, quantify the ambient complex dimension, and define polynomial convexity via the polynomial hull. Because Proposition 1.2 is presented as equivalent to Conjecture 1.1, it is appropriate to list that broader conjectural formulation as the sole alternate formulation.
